steps: Boiling the pasta: Bring plenty of water (about 2 liters) to a boil with coarse salt and add the 200g spaghetti. Boil for 8-9 minutes so it stays al dente, meaning it still has some bite, since it will finish cooking in the pan.

Reserving the pasta water: Before draining, reserve 1 cup of the starchy cooking water. IMPORTANT: this water is the secret of the recipe, as the starch binds the olive oil to the pasta and creates a creamy, glossy sauce without cream.
Preparing the aromatics: Cut the 5 garlic cloves into thin slices and finely chop the 1-2 hot chili peppers, so they gradually release their aroma into the oil.

Sautéing the garlic: Warm the 60ml olive oil over low heat and sauté the garlic and chili for 2-3 minutes until lightly golden. IMPORTANT: don't let the garlic burn, as it turns bitter and ruins the whole dish's flavor.

Combining with the pasta: Add the drained spaghetti to the pan along with a little of the cooking water and toss vigorously (shake the pan) for 1-2 minutes, so the oil emulsifies and the sauce comes together.
Serving: Add finely chopped fresh parsley and grated Parmesan, toss, and serve immediately while hot, so the sauce doesn't dry out.
aglio.plate: A nest of spaghetti, parsley, Parmesan.

steps: Grate the garlic or crush it in a mortar with salt.
Mix the mayonnaise, garlic, lemon juice and mustard.
Taste and adjust the salt and lemon.
Cover and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes to let the flavor develop.
Serve as a dip or accompaniment.
Mixing the dry ingredients: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt together in a bowl.
Mixing the wet ingredients: Beat the eggs with the milk, the melted butter and the vanilla in a second bowl.
Combining: Pour the wet into the dry and stir 10 times only, with a spoon.
Important: The batter must stay lumpy. Every extra stir develops gluten, and gluten turns pancakes flat and rubbery.
Resting: Rest the batter for 15 minutes. The baking powder starts working and bubbles form on the surface — this is what gives the height.
Heating the pan: Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and wipe it with a little butter using kitchen paper.
Important: Medium heat, never high. On a hot pan the outside burns while the inside stays raw batter.
Cooking: Pour a ladle per pancake and wait until bubbles appear over the whole surface and the edges look set — about 2 minutes.
Flipping: Flip once and cook for 1 minute more. Important: flip only once — a second flip deflates them.
Keeping warm: Stack them on a plate under a clean tea towel, which keeps them warm and soft while you cook the rest.
american_pancakes.plate: Stack 3-4 in a tower with maple syrup running down and butter on top.

ing: Almond extract (a few drops) for aroma
A few whole almonds, for decoration
steps: Preparing the almonds: Blanch the almonds, peel them, and grind them finely in a mill or food processor until they become almost flour-like.
Mixing the dry ingredients: In a large bowl, mix the ground almonds with the powdered sugar and lemon zest.
Whipping the egg whites: Whisk the egg whites with the granulated sugar until they form a meringue with a firm, glossy texture.
Combining the mixture: Gradually add the meringue to the almond mixture along with the orange blossom water and almond extract, gently kneading until the ingredients are well combined.
Important: The dough should be soft but not sticky to the touch; if it's too wet, add a little more powdered sugar, so the almond cookies hold their shape and don't spread during baking.
Shaping: Take small portions of dough and shape them into pears or crescents, placing an almond on top of each for decoration.
Baking: Place them on a parchment-lined baking tray and bake in a preheated oven at 150°C for 15-18 minutes, until lightly golden on the outside while staying soft inside.
Cooling and dusting: Let them cool completely and dust generously with powdered sugar before serving.
amygdalota.plate: Serve on a platter lined with doily paper, dusted with powdered sugar

steps: Cleaning the artichokes: Clean the 6 artichokes, removing the tough outer leaves and the fuzzy choke. Place them immediately in water with lemon juice. Important: the lemon water prevents oxidation, so the artichokes don't turn black before you cook them.
Preparing the vegetables: Cut the 4 carrots and 4 potatoes into thick pieces and shell the peas if using fresh ones (300g).
Sautéing: Sauté chopped onion in part of the 4 tbsp olive oil until softened and glossy, without taking on color. This sweetens it and builds a flavor base for the dish.
Adding the ingredients: Add the artichokes, carrots, potatoes and peas. Add water until nearly covered, along with the lemon juice and the remaining olive oil.

Slow cooking: Simmer over low heat for 35-40 minutes until the vegetables soften and the dish is left with its signature lemony sauce. Important: shake the pot instead of stirring with a spoon, so the artichokes and potatoes don't fall apart.
Finishing and serving: At the end, let the liquids reduce slightly. Add plenty of fresh dill and a little more lemon, then serve warm.
Beat the eggs with the milk. Add the crumbled anthotyro, mint, a little salt, and pepper.
Grease a baking pan and layer 3 phyllo sheets, brushing each sheet with oil.
Spread the filling evenly.
Cover with the remaining 3 phyllo sheets, brushing with oil. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake at 175°C for 40 minutes, until golden brown.
Sautéing the onions: In a pot with 4 tbsp olive oil, sauté the 2 finely chopped onions over medium heat for 4-5 minutes until softened and translucent, so they sweeten and build a flavor base.
Adding the vegetables: Add the 2 carrots cut into rounds and the 750g peas and stir for 2-3 minutes to coat them in the oil.
Adding the tomato: Add the 3 grated tomatoes, salt, pepper and 100ml water. Stir gently. Important: stir gently so the peas don't fall apart and keep their shape.
Slow cooking: Cover and simmer over low heat for 30 minutes until the peas become tender and the liquid reduces into an olive-oil-rich sauce.
Checking the liquid: If it dries out too soon, add a little hot water. The dish should stay juicy but not watery.
Finishing: At the end, add plenty of chopped fresh dill and stir, so it keeps its fresh aroma.
Serving: Let the peas rest for 10 minutes off the heat and serve lukewarm with feta and bread, as ladera dishes taste best not piping hot.
arakas_laderos.plate: With white bread and feta. A classic Greek olive-oil dish.

steps: Marinating: In a bowl, mix the juice of 3 lemons, 4 tbsp olive oil, 6 crushed garlic cloves and oregano. Rub the mixture all over the 1.5kg leg of lamb and refrigerate for at least 2 hours (ideally overnight), so the acidity of the lemon tenderizes the meat and the flavors penetrate deeply.
Preheating the oven: Preheat the oven to 190°C with top-bottom heat, so the meat cooks evenly.
Preparing the pan: Cut the 600g potatoes into wedges and arrange them in the roasting pan around the lamb. Pour over the marinade and add a little water so they don't dry out.
Roasting: Cover with foil and roast at 190°C for 75-80 minutes total. The initial covering keeps the juices in and cooks the meat until tender.

Turning halfway: At the 50-minute mark, turn the meat and potatoes and remove the foil, so they brown and develop a crispy crust. Important: if the liquids have dried up, add a little hot water so the potatoes don't burn.
Checking doneness: The lamb is ready when the meat pulls away easily from the bone. If needed, leave it a few more minutes.
Resting and serving: Remove the pan and let the meat rest for 10 minutes so the juices redistribute, then serve with the potatoes and pan juices.

ing: Leg or shoulder of lamb 1.5 kg
steps: Preparing the meat: Wash the lamb well and pat it dry with paper towels. Make small incisions all over the surface with a knife and insert pieces of garlic.

Marinating: In a bowl, mix the olive oil, lemon juice, mustard, oregano, salt and pepper. Rub the meat well with the mixture and let it marinate for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight in the refrigerator.
Potatoes: Peel the potatoes and cut them into slices or chunks. Arrange them around the meat in a baking pan and drizzle with a little olive oil, lemon juice, oregano and salt.
Important: Add the water or stock to the pan and cover it tightly with foil for the first hours of roasting; this way the meat steams, stays juicy and becomes tender without drying out.
First roasting: Roast in a preheated oven at 160°C for about 2 to 2.5 hours, covered, until the meat is tender and comes away easily from the bone.
Uncovering and browning: Remove the foil, raise the temperature to 200°C and roast for another 30-40 minutes, turning the potatoes, until the meat and potatoes are nicely browned.
Resting: Remove the pan from the oven and let the meat rest for 10 minutes before carving, so the juices settle.
Serving: Serve the lamb carved into portions together with the potatoes, and drizzle with the pan juices.
arni_fournou_patates.wine: Xinomavro from Naoussa or another full-bodied dry red wine.
arni_fournou_patates.plate: Serve on a plate with boiled greens or Greek village salad and fresh bread to enjoy with the pan juices.

steps: Marinating: Mix the juice of 1 lemon with 4 crushed garlic cloves, oregano, thyme and olive oil. Rub the mixture over the 1.2kg lamb shoulder pieces and let them sit for at least 1 hour, so the flavors penetrate and the meat becomes more tender.
Preparing the vegetables: Cut 4 potatoes, 2 peppers and 2 tomatoes into thick chunks so they hold together during the long roasting time.
Building the parcel: On a large sheet of parchment paper, arrange the lamb, potatoes, peppers, tomatoes, 4 garlic cloves and the 100g kefalotyri. Season with salt and pepper.

Sealing: Close the parchment tightly into a parcel, perhaps with a second layer or foil. Important: a tight seal traps the steam so the meat slow-cooks in its own juices and becomes wonderfully tender.
Slow roasting: Roast at 160°C for 2.5-3 hours. The low temperature and long cooking time make the meat so tender it melts in your mouth.
Browning: In the last 20 minutes, open the parchment on top so the meat browns and any excess liquid evaporates.
Serving: Serve the kleftiko right in the opened parchment with all its juices, so it stays hot and aromatic.
arni_kleftiko.plate: In the parchment, with melted kefalotyri and oregano.

steps: Marinating the night before: Open up the 10-12kg lamb and rub it thoroughly, inside and out, with coarse salt, pepper, plenty of oregano and thyme, the 10 garlic cloves, the juice of the 4 lemons and the 200ml olive oil. Important: marinating overnight lets the salt and aromatics penetrate deep into the meat, so the flavor isn't just skin-deep.

Trussing on the spit: Run the spit along the spine and tie the lamb very tightly with wire at the legs, shoulders and body. Tight trussing keeps the meat from hanging loose and turning unevenly over the fire, ensuring it cooks evenly.

Lighting the fire: At 8:00 in the morning, light the charcoal and let it burn down to embers with no flames before you start. Important: never roast over an open flame — it will char the outside while leaving the inside raw. You want steady heat from hot embers.
Steady turning: Position the lamb about 30cm from the fire and begin continuous, slow turning. This distance ensures slow cooking that renders the fat gradually and keeps the meat juicy.
Basting during roasting: Every 30-40 minutes, baste the lamb with a mixture of olive oil and lemon. This keeps the surface moist, helps it brown evenly and adds flavor with every layer.

Checking doneness: After about 3.5 hours the lamb should be evenly browned with a crispy skin. Cut into the thickest part of the thigh — if the juices run clear, it's ready. If they're pink, continue roasting.

Resting and carving: Take the lamb off the spit and let it rest for 15 minutes before carving. Resting allows the juices to redistribute through the meat, so they don't all run out as soon as you cut it, keeping it juicy.
arni_souvia.plate: Whole lamb, lemon, oregano. An Easter tradition!

ing: Chili flakes or hot pepper 1/2 tsp
steps: Preparing the lobster: Boil the lobster in salted water for 8-10 minutes until the shell turns red, let it cool and carefully remove the meat from the tail and claws, keeping the shell for the stock.
Lobster stock: Sauté the shells in a little olive oil for 5 minutes until fragrant, deglaze with a little water and simmer for 15 minutes, then strain and reserve the stock.
Sauce: In a wide pot, sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil until softened, deglaze with the wine and let the alcohol evaporate.

Important: Add the grated tomato and the lobster stock and simmer over low heat for 25-30 minutes uncovered, so the sauce thickens and the flavors concentrate - slow simmering is the secret to a deep taste of the sea.
Boiling the pasta: Boil the linguine in plenty of salted water until al dente, reserving half a glass of the cooking water.
Combining: Add the lobster meat, cut into pieces, to the sauce and warm through for 2-3 minutes without boiling hard, so the meat doesn't toughen.
Finishing: Add the drained pasta to the sauce, toss well, adding a little pasta water if needed, and serve immediately with parsley and chili flakes.
Serving: Divide among warm plates, placing the whole claws on top for an impressive presentation.
astakomakaronada.wine: White Assyrtiko from Santorini, cool and mineral, brings out the sweetness of the lobster.
astakomakaronada.plate: Serve in a deep white plate with the lobster claws on top, a little fresh parsley and a lemon wedge on the side.

steps: Boiling the eggs: Place the eggs in cold water and bring to the boil, then cook for exactly 10 minutes for a fully set yolk.
Cooling: Important: Plunge them straight into iced water for 5 minutes. This stops the cooking, prevents the grey-green ring around the yolk, and makes them peel cleanly.
Peeling: Peel them under running water — the stream gets under the membrane and lifts the shell off in pieces.
Halving: Cut them lengthwise with a knife wiped clean between each cut, so the whites stay neat.
Removing the yolks: Scoop out the yolks into a bowl and set the whites aside on the serving platter.
Making the filling: Mash the yolks with a fork until completely smooth, then mix in the mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice, dill, salt and pepper.
Checking the texture: The filling should be thick enough to hold its shape when piped. Important: too loose and it will slump out of the whites within minutes.
Filling: Pipe the mixture into the whites with a piping bag for a clean finish, or spoon it in generously.
Garnishing: Dust with paprika and top each half with a caper or a piece of olive.
Chilling: Chill for 30 minutes before serving, so the filling firms up and holds its shape.
avga_gemista.wine: A sparkling wine or a dry white as an appetiser.
avga_gemista.plate: Arrange on a flat platter in neat rows, dusted with paprika and scattered with dill.

steps: Cutting the sausage: Cut the 100g sausage (or apaki) into slices about half a centimeter thick, so they brown evenly.
Frying the sausage: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil and fry the slices for 2-3 minutes until browned and their aromatic fat renders out, which will flavor the eggs.
Cracking the eggs: Carefully crack the 4 eggs in next to the sausage. Important: crack each egg into a cup first if you're worried about breaking the yolk, then slide it gently into the pan.
Lowering the heat: Lower the heat so the whites set slowly without burning at the edges while the yolks stay runny.
Cooking: Cook for 2-3 minutes for a runny yolk or 4 minutes for well done. You can cover the pan to set the surface of the whites.
Serving: Sprinkle with salt and pepper at the end and serve immediately with fresh bread for dipping the yolk.
Cooking the broth and rice: Bring the 1.5L chicken broth to a boil, add the 100g rice, and cook for about 15 minutes until tender. A good broth is the foundation of flavor in the soup.
Whisking the eggs: In a bowl, whisk the 3 eggs well until frothy and gradually add the juice of 2 lemons while whisking. Whisking well gives a light, velvety avgolemono.

Tempering: Slowly add a few ladlefuls of hot broth into the egg mixture, whisking constantly. Important: the broth is added slowly with continuous whisking so the temperature of the eggs rises gradually and they don't curdle.

Combining with the soup: Lower or turn off the heat and pour the avgolemono into the pot, stirring gently. Important: do not boil the soup again after adding the avgolemono, or the eggs will curdle and ruin the texture.
Adjusting the seasoning: Taste and add salt, pepper, or a little extra lemon as preferred. The balance of tartness and salt gives the characteristic freshness.
Serving: Serve the soup immediately while hot and frothy, with freshly ground pepper on top. The avgolemono thickens over time, so it's best enjoyed fresh.
avgolemono_soupa.plate: With fresh bread. Classic Greek comfort food.

steps: Desalting: Soak the salt cod (600g) for 24-36 hours in cold water, changing the water 3-4 times a day. Important: frequent water changes are essential to remove the excess salt, otherwise the fish will remain unbearably salty.
Drying: Drain the cod well and pat dry with paper towels, so the coating adheres properly and doesn't cause the oil to spatter during frying.
Boiling the potatoes: Boil the 3 potatoes in their skins until tender, then peel them while still hot so the skordalia purées more easily and smoothly.

Skordalia: Mash the potatoes together with the 5 garlic cloves, gradually adding olive oil and the 2 tbsp of vinegar, until creamy. Important: add the oil gradually so the mixture emulsifies and doesn't split.
Coating and frying: Dust the cod with the cup of flour and fry in hot olive oil for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp.
Serving: Drain on paper towels and serve hot with the skordalia on the side and olives, for the classic flavor combination.
bakaliaro.plate: Cod with skordalia, olives, and greens.

ing: Sugar 1 tsp (to offset the tomato's acidity)
steps: Desalting: If using salt cod, soak it in cold water for 24 hours, changing the water 3-4 times, so the excess salt is removed. Important: Taste a small bite before cooking; if it's still very salty, soak it for a few more hours, otherwise the dish will come out unbearably salty.
Preparing the vegetables: Peel and slice the onions thinly and finely chop the garlic. Peel the potatoes and cut them into thick rounds or wedges.
Sautéing: In a wide pot, heat half the olive oil and sauté the onions over low heat until softened and glossy, without coloring. Add the garlic for a minute.
Tomato sauce: Add the grated tomatoes, bay leaf, sugar, salt and pepper and let the sauce simmer for 15-20 minutes until it thickens and the excess moisture cooks off.

Layering in the pan: Spread the potatoes over the bottom of a baking pan, season lightly with salt and pepper (less if the cod is salty) and pour over a little sauce. Place the cod pieces on top, skin-side down.

Baking: Cover with the remaining tomato sauce, drizzle with the rest of the olive oil and bake in a preheated oven at 190°C for 40-45 minutes, until the potatoes soften and the sauce caramelizes slightly at the edges. Important: Do not cover the pan with foil for the whole baking time, so the sauce reduces and develops depth of flavor.
Serving: Let the dish stand for 5-10 minutes out of the oven, sprinkle with fresh chopped parsley and serve hot.
bakaliaros_plaki.wine: Dry white Assyrtiko from Santorini or well-chilled retsina
bakaliaros_plaki.plate: Serve on an earthenware plate with a slice of local bread to mop up the sauce and a little fresh cabbage-and-carrot salad on the side

steps: Desalting the cod: Important: Soak the salt cod for 24-36 hours in the fridge, changing the water 5-6 times. Under-soaked cod is inedibly salty and cannot be corrected later.
Testing: Taste a small piece of the thickest part — it should be pleasantly savoury, not salty.
Cutting: Cut the cod into large portions and remove any large bones with tweezers.
Cleaning the leeks: Slice the leeks into thick rounds and wash them thoroughly between the layers, where soil always hides.
Sautéing the leeks: Sauté the leeks and the onion in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes, until they collapse and sweeten. This slow start is what makes the dish.
Adding the paste: Stir in the tomato paste and cook it for 1 minute, then add the grated tomato, the bay leaf and the sugar.
Simmering the sauce: Simmer for 20 minutes until the leeks are completely soft and the sauce has thickened.
Adding the cod: Lay the cod pieces on top of the sauce without stirring, cover and cook for 15 minutes only. Important: cod falls apart quickly, so it goes in last and is never stirred.
Seasoning: Season with pepper only — the cod brings its own salt. Taste before adding any.
Resting: Scatter over parsley and let it rest for 10 minutes off the heat before serving.
bakaliaros_prasa.wine: A dry white with acidity — Assyrtiko or Robola.
bakaliaros_prasa.plate: Serve the cod pieces whole on a bed of leeks in a deep plate, with sauce spooned over and bread.

steps: Preparing the filling: Mix the 300g ground walnuts with the 100g almonds, cinnamon and ground cloves. The spices give baklava its characteristic aromatic depth.

Layering the sheets: Butter 5-6 phyllo sheets one by one with melted butter and layer them on the bottom of the baking dish, then spread the filling. IMPORTANT: butter each sheet well so they turn crisp and don't stick together.
Layering: Continue alternating layers of buttered sheets and filling, keeping enough sheets for a rich top layer.
Scoring: Score the baklava diagonally into diamonds before baking. Scoring before baking is done while the sheets are still soft, so they don't shatter afterward and the syrup can soak in everywhere.
Baking: Bake in a preheated oven at 170°C for 45-50 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. The low temperature bakes the sheets evenly without burning.
Making the syrup: Boil the 300g sugar with the 200ml water and the 3 tbsp honey for a few minutes until the syrup thickens slightly.
Syruping: Pour hot syrup over cold baklava, or cold syrup over hot baklava. IMPORTANT: never both at the same temperature, or the baklava will turn soggy and lose its crispness.
Resting: Let the baklava absorb the syrup for at least 2 hours before cutting and serving, so it soaks evenly through every layer.
Cleaning the okra: Clean the 750g okra by carefully trimming the conical stem without opening the pod. Important: if you cut too deep, the okra will open up and become slimy during cooking.
Vinegar and sun: Sprinkle the okra with 1 tbsp vinegar and let sit in the sun for 30 minutes. The vinegar reduces the sliminess and helps them stay firm during cooking.
Sautéing the onion: In a pot or baking pan, heat the 4 tbsp olive oil and sauté the 1 finely chopped onion until softened and translucent.
Adding the okra: Add the okra on top of the onion without stirring, so the pods don't break and keep their shape.
Tomato and seasoning: Add the 400g grated tomato, half a teaspoon of sugar, salt and pepper. The sugar balances the tomato's acidity.
Slow cooking: Simmer over low heat for 40 minutes without stirring, only gently shaking the pot, so the okra doesn't fall apart. Serve lukewarm with fresh bread.

ing: Dulce de leche or condensed milk 400 g
steps: Crush the biscuits to fine crumbs and mix them with the melted butter until they look like wet sand.
Press the mixture firmly into a tart tin, base and sides, using the back of a glass to compact it evenly.
Refrigerate the base for 30 minutes to set. Important: an unchilled base crumbles the moment you cut the first slice.
Spread the dulce de leche over the base in an even layer.
Slice the bananas and arrange them over the caramel, overlapping slightly.
Important: Toss the banana slices in a little lemon juice first, or they will darken and look unappetising within the hour.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar to firm peaks and spread it over the bananas in generous swirls.
Grate dark chocolate over the top and refrigerate for 2 hours before serving.
banoffee.plate: Cut into portions with a hot knife so the three layers show cleanly.

ing: Olive oil or sunflower oil for frying 1/2 liter
steps: Cleaning: Clean the red mullet by scaling from tail to head, gut them with a small cut in the belly, and rinse very well with cold water. Drain.

Drying: Lay the mullet on paper towels and dry them thoroughly, inside and out. Important: the fish must be completely dry before flouring, since moisture makes the oil spatter and prevents a crisp crust from forming.
Salting: Salt the mullet with coarse salt a few minutes before frying, not earlier, so they don't release liquid and soften.
Flouring: Pour the flour onto a shallow plate and roll each mullet to coat it evenly. Shake off the excess flour so it doesn't burn in the oil.
Heating the oil: Heat plenty of oil in a deep skillet over high heat (about 175-180°C). Test by dropping in a little flour: if it sizzles immediately, the oil is ready.
Frying: Fry the mullet in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp. Don't overcrowd the pan, or the temperature will drop.
Draining: Remove with a slotted spatula and let them drain on paper towels to remove excess oil.
Serving: Serve immediately, hot, with plenty of lemon juice, freshly ground pepper, and chopped parsley.
barbounia.wine: Dry white, well chilled, or ouzo.
barbounia.plate: Serve with lemon wedges, boiled greens, or a refreshing village salad.

steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the flour and whisk quickly for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Gradually add the milk, whisking constantly.
Stir until it thickens (8-10 minutes).
Season with salt and pepper, and add the nutmeg.
Cutting the meat: Cut the beef into large 4-5 cm cubes. Important: do not cut them small — long cooking shrinks them and small pieces fall apart into threads.
Drying: Pat the cubes completely dry and season with salt and pepper. A wet surface will never brown.
Rendering the bacon: Cook the diced bacon in a heavy pot until crisp, then lift it out and reserve.
Searing the beef: Sear the cubes in the bacon fat in small batches, so the pot stays hot and each piece gets a dark crust. This step defines the final colour of the dish.
Sautéing the vegetables: Add the carrots and onions, sauté for 5 minutes, add the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute more.
Adding flour: Dust with the flour and stir for 2 minutes to cook out its raw taste.
Deglazing with wine: Pour in the wine, scrape the bottom of the pot and let it boil for 5 minutes to drive off the alcohol.
Slow cooking: Add the stock, the bay leaves, the thyme and the bacon, cover and cook over very low heat for 2 hours and 30 minutes, or in the oven at 160°C.
Adding the mushrooms: Sauté the mushrooms in butter until golden and stir them in for the last 20 minutes.
Checking: The dish is ready when a piece of meat gives way under a fork with no resistance at all.
Reducing: If needed, uncover and reduce over medium heat until the sauce is glossy and clings to the meat.
beef_bourguignon.wine: A Burgundy Pinot Noir, or the same wine used in the pot.
beef_bourguignon.plate: Serve in a deep bowl over mashed potato, with the onions and mushrooms arranged on top.
